key_insight: A combined CEL simulation and ANN framework can accurately predict friction stir welding quality in HDPE and identify safe process windows for defect-free joints.
engineering_relevance: This work offers practical process maps for optimizing rotational speed, welding speed, and bottom preheating to reduce defects, stabilize forces, and improve weld reliability in thermoplastic joining.
method: 3D coupled Eulerian-Lagrangian (CEL) model of HDPE FSW under varied speeds and preheating
Two multilayer perceptron ANNs trained on experimental temperature and axial-force histories
Validation against experiments to map defect-free and defective welding conditions
evidence_signal: The ANN models achieved high predictive accuracy with R2 between 0.91 and 0.99, while the CEL model matched experimental void formation, thermal behavior, and axial force trends.
watch_item: The process map is based on the tested HDPE parameter range, so transfer to different tool geometries, thicknesses, or polymers may require retraining and revalidation.
paper_title: Computational and machine learning modelling approaches for weld quality predictions in friction stir welding of high-density polyethylene
